headline: Notebandi's missing money
captionHeadline: The note ban was meant to trap black money. Then 99.3% of the banned cash walked straight back into the banks.
summary: ₹15.41 lakh crore of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes were cancelled overnight in November 2016. By the RBI's own count, ₹15.31 lakh crore came back. Only about ₹10,720 crore never returned.
forYou: If the black money never stayed in cash, it was already somewhere else. Gold. Property. Abroad.
cta: Send this to the uncle who still says "notebandi finished black money".

slides.label: THE PLAN
slides.title: Trap the cash overnight
slides.body: 8 November 2016, 8 pm. 86% of India's cash stops being money at midnight. The idea: black money hoarders can't bring it back without getting caught.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: So where did the black money go?
slides.body: If 99.3% came back, either there was far less black cash than believed, or it was laundered back in. Either way, the cash pile everyone imagined was never found.

slides.label: SEND THIS
slides.title: Notebandi, by the numbers
slides.body: Send this to the uncle who still believes the note ban worked.

headline: ₹351 crore cash
source: Income Tax Department searches, Dec 2023 (as reported by PTI and others)
captionHeadline: ₹351 crore. In cash. Officers needed 36 counting machines and about 10 days to count it.
summary: In December 2023, Income Tax searches on a liquor business group in Odisha found cash stacked in cupboards and bags. It was reported as the biggest cash seizure by any agency in a single operation in India.
forYou: Even the counting machines struggled to keep up.
cta: Send this to someone who thinks they work hard for their money.

slides.label: THE RAID
slides.title: It started as a tax search
slides.body: Income Tax teams searched premises linked to a liquor group in Odisha and Jharkhand. Then they opened the cupboards.

slides.label: THE COUNT
slides.title: What it took to count it

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: All of it in cash
slides.body: Not bank balances. Not shares. Physical notes, in an economy that had already gone through a note ban to kill exactly this.

headline: Gold in toilet
source: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, via PIB, 25 Jul 2026
captionHeadline: About 12 kg of gold bars, hidden behind the ceiling panels of a plane's rear toilet.
summary: That was one catch on a flight from Addis Ababa. In a single week, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence says it seized 27 kg of smuggled gold, including gold dust hidden in wax, and arrested 12 people.
forYou: The gold flew in. The smuggler didn't have to carry it.
cta: Send this to the friend who always takes forever in the airplane toilet.

slides.label: THE HIDING PLACE
slides.title: Behind the ceiling panel
slides.body: Officers opened the ceiling panels of the rear lavatory on a flight from Addis Ababa and found gold bars packed inside.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: Gold dust in wax
slides.body: Other catches that week were gold turned into dust and hidden in wax, so it passes as something else.

slides.label: SEND THIS
slides.title: Check the ceiling next time
slides.body: Send this to your travel buddy.

headline: Votes for sale
captionHeadline: ₹8,889 crore. That's what was seized to buy votes before the 2024 Lok Sabha election had even finished.
summary: Cash, liquor, drugs, precious metals and freebies were picked up by enforcement teams by 18 May 2024, with phases still left to vote. Drugs alone made up about 45% of it.
forYou: This is only what got caught.
cta: Send this to the friend who says "my one vote doesn't matter". Someone thought it was worth paying for.

slides.label: THE HAUL
slides.title: Seized before you voted
slides.body: Every election, flying squads stop cars, raid godowns and check bags. In 2024 they found more than ever before.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: This is only what got caught
slides.body: ₹8,889 crore was seized by 18 May 2024, with phases still to go. What wasn't seized never shows up in any report.

headline: Narco hawala trail
captionHeadline: A ₹100 crore drug-money trail, running through bank accounts in Mizoram towns and out to suppliers in Myanmar.
summary: The Enforcement Directorate says it froze 1,424 accounts, arrested 18 people, attached ₹17.82 crore and found 500 detonators in its hawala probe. All accused are innocent until proven guilty.
forYou: 1,424 accounts. Most of them in other people's names.
cta: Send this to the friend who binge-watches Narcos.

slides.label: THE ROUTE
slides.title: Follow the money
slides.body: Drug money collected in Mizoram, the ED says, was pushed through local bank accounts and moved out through hawala to suppliers across the border in Myanmar.

slides.label: THE BUST
slides.title: What the ED says it found

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: Hawala leaves no receipt
slides.body: Money never actually crosses the border. One side pays, the other side hands out cash, and the books are settled in trust.

headline: Swiss bank money
source: Swiss National Bank annual data, released 19 Jun 2026
captionHeadline: ₹36,793 crore. Money linked to India sitting in Swiss banks at the end of 2025.
summary: The total (CHF 3.25 billion) fell 8%, but customer deposits jumped more than 50% to CHF 524 million. Swiss authorities say these figures "cannot be considered as black money": most of it belongs to banks and companies.
forYou: Officially, it's not black money. So whose is it?
cta: Send this to the friend who still says "Swiss account".

slides.label: THE CATCH
slides.title: Swiss say: not black money
slides.body: Most of this money sits with banks and Indian companies' branches. Swiss authorities say it "cannot be considered as black money".

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.title: Deposits still jumped 50%
slides.body: Even as the total fell, money held by customers in India rose more than 50% to CHF 524 million in one year.
